taxonomyNote: NatureServe (Nicholson 2025) recognizes subspecies campi, flavilenta and maculata; TPWD's page covers the subspecies H. m. maculata (northern earless lizard).
fieldMarks: Striped or speckled back; two black bars on each side of the belly, sometimes described as bars near the armpits; up to about 13 cm total length (CPW; TPWD).
Mature male: two enlarged scales under the tail behind the vent, black blue-edged belly bars, possible yellowish wash on the sides (CPW).
Mature female: belly bars lack blue edging; breeding females show yellow-orange on the throat, head and neck and orange on the sides (CPW).
behavior: Mainly diurnal, but may be active in the evening and at night in hot weather (NatureServe).
Takes cover in rodent burrows or burrows into sand (CPW).
Active March-October in the north; lays 1-2 clutches between April and September (NatureServe).
habitat: Sparsely vegetated sandy or gravelly ground: sandhills, prairie-dog towns, washes, streambanks, dunes, sagebrush flats and open prairie (CPW; NatureServe).
range: Southern South Dakota to central Texas, southwest to southeastern Utah and Arizona, and south to Jalisco and Guanajuato, Mexico (NatureServe).
